beats.headline: The bad one
beats.text: Katia vomits again, and Carl sends Mordecai a private message: tell me about these drugs. Mordecai lists them. Travis Priest, a strong painkiller, cured first. Creamsicle Charm, ground-up fairy wings. The blitz sticks. Finally there is Glory Bound, which she has taken only once, thank goodness. It is the bad one, by far the most addictive: it puts her in a coma and lets her relive a memory, like blitz but much stronger. Without more she will slowly go insane, unable to tell then from now. So the cure is a bad trip of Glory Bound, a regular dose with some stuff added, and she will have to relive one of her worst memories.

beats.headline: One jar, two treatments
beats.text: In a new field hospital at the base, Mordecai sets a fizzing green jar on the counter, thick carbonated slime: two hits of Glory Bound compounded with a subdermal gel and a potion called Tough Love, brewed since the last floor and now in its short window of potency. Carl's dose gets Removal Order as well, so that, Mordecai hopes, he will visit the spider's memories instead of his own, and at the end he can choose to lock Shi Maria in hers. The drug began outside the inner system as a medication for learning difficult tasks, and it lingers in the dungeon in quests and traps. Mordecai rubs the gel on Katia's neck and slops a cold, fizzing blob on Carl.

beats.headline: Waking up somewhere else
beats.text: Carl blinks awake on the other side of the map, in what he thinks is the high elf castle, with no idea how he got there. The memory they shared is a jumble, like a real dream. He suspects Katia's treatment worked. His own worked, sort of: the spider's husband, a god called Hapanzi, reappeared at the end and told him he has her now, good and trapped, and not to set her free unless all is lost. The eye on Carl's chest is still a tattoo, but now he can see from it when it opens.
